# Add a `--json` flag to `faff config get`

## WHY
Scripts that read faff config currently parse human-formatted stdout. A machine-readable mode removes that brittleness.

## WHAT
`faff config get <key> --json` prints `{ "key": <key>, "value": <resolved>, "source": "file|default" }` to stdout; exit codes unchanged.

## HOW
**Chosen:** extend the existing `config get` handler in `bin/faff` with a `--json` branch that wraps the already-resolved value; no new resolution path. The resolver already returns `{ value, source }` internally, so the flag only changes the print format.

## DONE
- [ ] `faff config get tracking.team_key --json` prints the documented object
- [ ] an absent key prints `{"value": null, "source": "default"}` and exits 3 (unchanged)
- [ ] a unit test asserts the JSON shape and the unchanged exit codes

Every decision is marked, no open questions remain, and DONE mirrors the body.
